newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Wednesday, June 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Wednesday, June 18.

text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Foreign minister Lamberto Dini, attending the European Union summit in Amsterdam, said Italy will meet tough crietria in 1997 for aspiring founder members of the European single currency. Prime minister Romano Prodi added the country would need no flexible interpretation of the Maastricht treaty to win membership of EMU (all).
* Hard left Communist Refoundation party said it would stick to its own line in negotiations between the centre-left government, unions and employers over welfare reforms (all).

* Deputy prime minister Enrico Micheli said the 10 to 15 trillion lire spending cuts for 1998 labour minister Tiziano Treu was referring to on Tuesday evening meant the entire three-year economic programme known as the DPEF, not just relating to welfare spending cuts (La Repubblica).

* Insurer Generali said it was setting up a fund of $ 12 million to honour the victims of the holocaust, with this money to be paid out over the next 12 years to organisations supporting victims (all).

* Anders Scharp, chairman of Sweden's Electrolux, the world's largest supplier of household appliances, said the group's restructuring programme, which includes the closure of about 25,000 firms in Europe and some 12,000 layoffs, did not include any cut to the Italian sector (all).

* In an interview, Treasury minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said he was confident Italy would make the grade for EMU and Euro would be "broad and strong". Ciampi also said he believed political forces would soon find an agreement on social spending cuts (Sole 24 Ore).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
